In the Hà Giang highlands, Vietnam Plus describes a small free-range pig of about 4 to 10 kg, carried to market under the arm and fed on corn, sweet potato, cassava, roots, and forest greens. It is cooked whole as quay, or grilled, steamed, or stir-fried. The favored pieces are lòng dồi and belly still on the rib, steamed, with salt pounded with green chili and mắc khén. Some places grill the meat in a bamboo tube. Skin crisp, little fat, lean meat that is firm. It may be eaten with rượu ngô or rượu táo mèo.
